strongest_verified_theorem: For a countable undirected simple bounded-degree graph, vertex rates 0<p_v<=P, reinforcement 0<=alpha<1 and arbitrary deterministic positive integer initial edge counts finite on each edge, there is a unique strictly positive equilibrium and N_e(t)/t converges to it simultaneously almost surely in every edge coordinate. No uniform lower rate or initial-count bound is needed.
stochastic_family_independence: INDEPENDENT_DERIVATION.md was saved before historical audit conclusions were read. Deterministic dependencies were then crosschecked, not represented as a second independent deterministic-family review.
literal_counterexample: The integer line with unit vertex rates, 0<alpha<1, and either 2/0 alternating edge array; all denominators are positive. The constant-one array is another equilibrium.
exact_remaining_gap: No gap in the candidate positive theorem. It cannot prove literal uniqueness among all nonnegative equilibria because that statement is false. The positive formulation must remain explicitly corrected. Current priority/novelty and preprint readiness require separate audits.
